aspects.says: Arrow labels never fall through, in a statement or an expression; colon labels fall through even in a switch expression, until a yield.
basis: section:An Arrow Label Runs One Arm and Never Falls Through; a Colon Label Still Does, Even in an Expression

aspects.says: A switch expression over an enum that names every constant and has no default stops compiling when a constant is added; a default arm lets the new constant through.
basis: section:A Switch Expression Must Cover Every Input, and an Enum Covered Without default Is Rechecked at Every Compile

aspects.says: A constant added to the enum after the switch was compiled reaches the default javac generated, which throws MatchException (IncompatibleClassChangeError when compiled for release 20 or earlier).
basis: section:A Constant Added After Compilation Reaches the Switch as MatchException

aspects.says: A switch statement over an enum is not treated as covering every constant, so a variable it assigns in every arm is still not definitely assigned; a switch expression gives one value with no default.
basis: section:A Switch Expression Is a Value, So Every Arm Must Produce One

aspects.says: Assigned to a reference type, a switch expression boxes each arm on its own, while a numeric ?: and a switch under var promote the arms to a common numeric type.
basis: section:A Switch Expression Is a Value, So Every Arm Must Produce One

aspects.says: A block arm gives its value with yield; return and break out of a switch expression, and a block arm without a value, are compile errors.
basis: section:A Block Arm Hands Out Its Value With yield; return and break Can't Leave a Switch Expression
